# Endpoint index

Source: <https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/openapi.json>, the API reference.

Every path is under `/v1`. The API reference's server is the sandbox, `https://gateway-sandbox.matambaintelligence.com`. The live host comes with your live keys: never guess it.

| Method | Path | What it does | Key scope | `Idempotency-Key` | Reference |

## What each endpoint does

### `GET /v1/accounts`

Returns the accounts this API key can trade for, in order of account code, a page at a time. Call this first to check your setup. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `limit` (query): integer, min 1, max 100. The number of items to return.
- `cursor` (query): string, min length 1. The `next_cursor` from the previous page, unchanged.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/accounts/{account}`

Returns one of your accounts from our records, without asking the broker. Takes no query parameters. For what the broker holds in it, read its balance and positions. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `account` (path, required): AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$`. One of your account codes, from GET /v1/accounts.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `POST /v1/orders`

Stores the order, then sends it to the exchange once. If an order ends in `uncertain`, we don't send it again. Retrieve it, or wait for its event, until it resolves. Requires the `trade` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `Idempotency-Key` (header, required): string, pattern `^[!-~]+$`, min length 1, max length 255. A key you choose to identify this request. Send the same key every time you retry the request. Once used, a key stays tied to that request permanently. It must be printable ASCII with no spaces, and we compare it byte for byte. Send the header only once.


Responses: `200`, `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `409`, `413`, `415`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/orders`

Returns your orders, newest first. If you place an order while you paginate, it appears before the first page and doesn't shift the pages that follow. Filters narrow the list and can be combined. Keep the same filters for every page. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `limit` (query): integer, min 1, max 100. The number of items to return.
- `cursor` (query): string, min length 1. The `next_cursor` from the previous page, unchanged.
- `account` (query): AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$`. Only orders for this account.
- `state` (query): OrderState (`sending`, `pending`, `partially_filled`, `filled`, `uncertain`, `rejected`, `refused`, `cancelled`, `expired`). Only orders in this state.
- `symbol` (query): string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,20}$`. Only orders for this symbol. Letter case doesn't matter.
- `client_reference` (query): ClientReference: string, pattern `^[!-~]{1,64}$`, min length 1, max length 64. Only the ones you sent with this `client_reference`, matched exactly.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `POST /v1/orders/estimate`

Returns the broker's estimate of an order's total: for a buy, what it would cost, and for a sell, what you'd receive. The estimate is indicative. Send the same body you'd use to place the order. This doesn't place or store an order, and you don't need an `Idempotency-Key`. Requires the `trade` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).


Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `413`, `415`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/orders/{id}`

Returns the order, including everything the exchange has reported about it. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `id` (path, required): string, pattern `^ord_[a-z2-7]{20}$`. The order's `id`.

Responses: `200`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `DELETE /v1/orders/{id}`

Requests a cancel of a `pending` or `partially_filled` limit order. Only limit orders can be cancelled. A `202` means the broker accepted the request, not that the order is cancelled: the order then moves to `cancelled`, or to `filled` if it fills before the cancel takes effect. Wait for the event, or retrieve the order. Requires the `trade` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `id` (path, required): string, pattern `^ord_[a-z2-7]{20}$`. The order's `id`.

Responses: `202`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/events`

Returns every change to your orders, applications and allocations, oldest first, whether or not your webhook endpoint accepted it. We keep events for 30 days. Store the last `next_cursor` and pass it as `cursor` next time. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `limit` (query): integer, min 1, max 100. The number of items to return.
- `cursor` (query): string, min length 1. The `next_cursor` from the previous page, unchanged.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `POST /v1/applications`

Sends your customer's application to the broker once. We pass the identity details through without storing or logging them. If an application ends in `uncertain`, we don't send it again. Then send its four documents with `PUT /v1/applications/{id}/documents/{type}`. Requires the `apply` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `Idempotency-Key` (header, required): string, pattern `^[!-~]+$`, min length 1, max length 255. A key you choose to identify this request. Send the same key every time you retry the request. Once used, a key stays tied to that request permanently. It must be printable ASCII with no spaces, and we compare it byte for byte. Send the header only once.

Body: `application/json`, ApplicationRequest.

Responses: `200`, `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `409`, `413`, `415`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/applications`

Returns your applications, newest first. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `limit` (query): integer, min 1, max 100. The number of items to return.
- `cursor` (query): string, min length 1. The `next_cursor` from the previous page, unchanged.
- `client_reference` (query): ClientReference: string, pattern `^[!-~]{1,64}$`, min length 1, max length 64. Only the ones you sent with this `client_reference`, matched exactly.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/applications/{id}`

Returns the application's current state. Once it's `opened`, you can trade for the account in `account`. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `id` (path, required): string, pattern `^app_[a-z2-7]{20}$`. The application's `id`.

Responses: `200`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `PUT /v1/applications/{id}/documents/{type}`

Sends one of the application's four documents to the broker: the file itself as the body, a JPEG or PNG smaller than 1,000,000 bytes and at most 8,000 pixels wide and high. We check that the file is whole, send it to the broker in the same request, and keep no copy. The same file sent again once the broker has it isn't sent twice; one whose earlier answer was unconfirmed is sent again. A different file for a type the broker has, or whose earlier file is unconfirmed, is refused. At most two of your documents are on their way to the broker at once. Send documents while the application is `documents_required` or `submitted`; the fourth makes it `submitted`. Requires the `apply` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `id` (path, required): string, pattern `^app_[a-z2-7]{20}$`. The application's `id`.
- `type` (path, required): DocumentType (`photo`, `government_id`, `utility_bill`, `signature`). Which of the four documents.

Body: `image/jpeg`, string, binary.
Body: `image/png`, string, binary.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `413`, `415`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/wallet`

Returns your wallet. Each figure is a ledger sum, all read at the same moment. Takes no parameters. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/wallet/transfers`

Returns every entry in your wallet's ledger, newest first: credits from your payments, the reserve, booking or return of each allocation, and the hold, payment, release or return of each withdrawal. Entries are never changed or removed, so a page never shifts. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `limit` (query): integer, min 1, max 100. The number of items to return.
- `cursor` (query): string, min length 1. The `next_cursor` from the previous page, unchanged.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `POST /v1/allocations`

Moves money from your wallet to the balance of one of your accounts at the broker, and it's booked only once. We reserve the amount in the same step that checks your wallet. If an allocation ends in `uncertain`, the amount stays reserved and we don't send it again. Requires the `fund` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `Idempotency-Key` (header, required): string, pattern `^[!-~]+$`, min length 1, max length 255. A key you choose to identify this request. Send the same key every time you retry the request. Once used, a key stays tied to that request permanently. It must be printable ASCII with no spaces, and we compare it byte for byte. Send the header only once.

Body: `application/json`, AllocationRequest.

Responses: `200`, `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `409`, `413`, `415`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/allocations`

Returns your allocations, newest first. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `limit` (query): integer, min 1, max 100. The number of items to return.
- `cursor` (query): string, min length 1. The `next_cursor` from the previous page, unchanged.
- `client_reference` (query): ClientReference: string, pattern `^[!-~]{1,64}$`, min length 1, max length 64. Only the ones you sent with this `client_reference`, matched exactly.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/allocations/{id}`

Returns the allocation's current state. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `id` (path, required): string, pattern `^alc_[a-z2-7]{20}$`. The allocation's `id`.

Responses: `200`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/reference/banks`

Returns the broker's list of banks. Use one of these codes as an application's `bank`. Takes no parameters. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/reference/states`

Returns the broker's list of states. Use these codes for an application's `state` and `state_of_origin`. Takes no parameters. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/reference/states/{state}/lgas`

Returns the broker's local government areas (LGAs) for one state. Use one of these codes as an application's `lga_of_origin`. Takes no query parameters. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `state` (path, required): string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$`. A state code from GET /v1/reference/states.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/balance`

Returns the account's balance as the broker reports it. Takes no query parameters. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `account` (path, required): AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$`. One of your account codes, from GET /v1/accounts.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `409`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/limits`

Returns each of your limits and how much of it you've used, counted the way the limit counts it. `remaining` is what a request can use at this moment. Takes no parameters. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `POST /v1/keys/revoke`

Ends the key you send in the `Authorization` header, at once. Use it the moment a key leaks, at any hour. Any key can revoke itself, whatever its scopes, and from any address, including one a live key isn't registered for. The answer is `204` whether the key worked, was already revoked or was never issued, so it never confirms that a key is real. To check, send any request with the key from one of your servers: `401` means it no longer works. Your other keys keep working, and a request the key started before you revoked it still finishes. Takes no body.

Responses: `204`, `401`, `429`, `500`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/positions`

Returns the account's positions as the broker reports them. Takes no query parameters. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `account` (path, required): AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$`. One of your account codes, from GET /v1/accounts.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `409`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/trades`

Returns buy and sell fills with a trade date from `from` to `to`, newest first. A range can include at most 1,000 records. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `from` (query): string, date. The first trade date, in West Africa Time (WAT). Defaults to 30 days before `to`. Can't be after `to`.
- `to` (query): string, date. The last trade date, in West Africa Time (WAT). Defaults to today. Can't be after today.
- `account` (path, required): AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$`. One of your account codes, from GET /v1/accounts.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `409`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

### `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/contract-notes`

Returns settled trades with their charges, for trades dated from `from` to `to`, newest first. A range can include at most 1,000 records. Requires the `read` [scope](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security#scopes).

Parameters:

- `from` (query): string, date. The first trade date, in West Africa Time (WAT). Defaults to 30 days before `to`. Can't be after `to`.
- `to` (query): string, date. The last trade date, in West Africa Time (WAT). Defaults to today. Can't be after today.
- `account` (path, required): AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$`. One of your account codes, from GET /v1/accounts.

Responses: `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `409`, `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, and `default` (the shared error shape).

## Request bodies

### OrderRequest

`OrderRequest`. Send numbers as JSON numbers, not quoted strings. We reject unknown fields and any field that appears twice, even with different letter case.

| Field | Required | Type and rule | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | Yes | AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$` | An account code. Case-insensitive on input, and returned in uppercase. |
| `symbol` | Yes | string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,20}$` | The exchange's symbol, treated as uppercase. The exchange decides whether the symbol exists. |
| `side` | Yes | OrderSide (`buy`, `sell`) | `buy` or `sell`. |
| `quantity` | Yes | integer, int64, min 1, max 100000000 | The number of shares, as a whole number. At least 1. The broker doesn't publish a minimum of its own. If the broker refuses a quantity, the order comes back `order_rejected` with `reject_reason` `rejected_by_exchange`. |
| `type` | Yes | OrderType (`limit`, `market`) | An ETF takes limit orders only. Shares take limit and market orders. The broker rejects a market order on an ETF with `reject_reason` set to `etf_limit_orders_only`. A market order is priced at the day's price limit: the upper limit for a buy, the lower limit for a sell. |
| `time_in_force` | Yes | TimeInForce (`day`, `gtc`, `ioc`, `fok`) | `day`: good for the current trading session only. `gtc`: good till cancelled. `ioc`: immediate or cancel. `fok`: fill or kill. We accept every `type` with every `time_in_force`. The broker decides which combinations it supports, and rejects the rest as `order_rejected` with a `reject_reason`. If it refuses an order with a reason it doesn't publish, the order is `uncertain` until our operations team reconciles it. |
| `price_kobo` | No | integer, int64, min 1, max 1000000000 | The limit price in kobo, so ₦475.00 is 47500. Required for a limit order. Omit it for a market order. |
| `client_reference` | No | ClientReference: string, pattern `^[!-~]{1,64}$`, min length 1, max length 64 | Your own reference for this, such as your internal ID, so you can find it again. 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces, matched exactly. We store it and return it. It's part of the request an `Idempotency-Key` stands for, so a retry with a different `client_reference` returns `409`. Never put personal data in it: no names, phone numbers, email addresses, BVN, NIN or account numbers of your customers. |

### ApplicationRequest

`ApplicationRequest`. We check that every required field is there; that each field is at most 200 characters, trimmed at both ends, with no control or invisible characters; that dates are real dates on or after 1900-01-01 and not in the future; that `gender` is `M` or `F`; that `bvn` and `nin` are 11 digits; and that `state`, `state_of_origin`, `lga_of_origin` and `bank` are shaped like the codes in the reference lists. The broker checks each against its lists, and everything else, and answers a field it can't accept with `422 application_rejected`, `reject_reason` `invalid_field`, and `param` naming the field. We reject unknown fields and any field that appears twice, even with different letter case.

| Field | Required | Type and rule | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `first_name` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The customer's first name. |
| `middle_name` | No | string, max length 200 | The customer's middle name, if they have one. |
| `last_name` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The customer's last name. |
| `gender` | Yes | string, one of `M`, `F` | `M` or `F`. |
| `date_of_birth` | Yes | string, date | Must be on or after 1900-01-01, and no later than today in West Africa Time (WAT). |
| `email` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The customer's email address. The broker checks it. In the sandbox, use a new value for each application: the sandbox's broker refuses one it has already accepted, from any partner. |
| `phone` | Yes | string, pattern `^(\+234\|0)[0-9]{10}$`, min length 1, max length 200 | The customer's phone number: a Nigerian number, `0` and 10 digits, or `+234` and the same 10 digits. We send it to the broker as `0` and 10 digits, which the broker asks for. |
| `mothers_maiden_name` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The customer's mother's maiden name. The broker's document marks it optional, but the broker refuses an application without one, so we require it. |
| `street` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The street of the customer's home address. |
| `city` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The city of the customer's home address. |
| `state` | Yes | string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$` | A code from GET /v1/reference/states. |
| `postcode` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The postcode of the customer's home address. |
| `state_of_origin` | Yes | string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$` | A code from GET /v1/reference/states. |
| `lga_of_origin` | Yes | string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$` | A code from GET /v1/reference/states/{state}/lgas. |
| `next_of_kin_name` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The name of the customer's next of kin. |
| `next_of_kin_phone` | Yes | string, pattern `^(\+234\|0)[0-9]{10}$`, min length 1, max length 200 | The phone number of the customer's next of kin, written as `phone` is. |
| `next_of_kin_relationship` | No | string, max length 200 | How the next of kin is related to the customer. |
| `next_of_kin_address` | No | string, max length 200 | The address of the customer's next of kin. |
| `bank` | Yes | string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$` | A code from GET /v1/reference/banks. |
| `bank_account_name` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The name on the customer's bank account at `bank`. |
| `bank_account_number` | Yes | string, min length 1, max length 200 | The customer's account number at `bank`. |
| `bank_account_opened` | Yes | string, date | Can't be before `date_of_birth` or after today in West Africa Time (WAT). |
| `bvn` | Yes | string, pattern `^[0-9]{11}$` | The customer's Bank Verification Number: 11 digits. In the sandbox, use a new value for each application: the sandbox's broker refuses one it has already accepted, from any partner. |
| `nin` | No | string, pattern `^[0-9]{11}$` | The customer's National Identification Number: 11 digits. |
| `tax_id` | No | string, max length 200 | The customer's tax identification number. |
| `client_reference` | No | ClientReference: string, pattern `^[!-~]{1,64}$`, min length 1, max length 64 | Your own reference for this, such as your internal ID, so you can find it again. 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces, matched exactly. We store it and return it. It's part of the request an `Idempotency-Key` stands for, so a retry with a different `client_reference` returns `409`. Never put personal data in it: no names, phone numbers, email addresses, BVN, NIN or account numbers of your customers. |

### AllocationRequest

`AllocationRequest`. We reject unknown fields and any field that appears twice, even with different letter case.

| Field | Required | Type and rule | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | Yes | AccountCode: string, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}$` | An account code. Case-insensitive on input, and returned in uppercase. |
| `amount_kobo` | Yes | integer, int64, min 1, max 10000000000 | The amount in kobo, as a whole number: at least 1 kobo, and at most ₦100,000,000. The broker doesn't publish a minimum of its own. If the broker refuses an amount, the allocation comes back `allocation_rejected` with `reject_reason` `invalid_amount`. |
| `client_reference` | No | ClientReference: string, pattern `^[!-~]{1,64}$`, min length 1, max length 64 | Your own reference for this, such as your internal ID, so you can find it again. 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces, matched exactly. We store it and return it. It's part of the request an `Idempotency-Key` stands for, so a retry with a different `client_reference` returns `409`. Never put personal data in it: no names, phone numbers, email addresses, BVN, NIN or account numbers of your customers. |

## Money fields

Every field whose name ends `_kobo` is an integer in kobo. Every field ending `_kobo_decimal` is a decimal string of kobo: parse it with a decimal type, never a float.

| Object | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OrderRequest` | `price_kobo` | The limit price in kobo, so ₦475.00 is 47500. Required for a limit order. Omit it for a market order. |
| `Order` | `price_kobo` | The limit price in kobo. Null for a market order. |
| `Order` | `average_fill_price_kobo_decimal` | The average price the filled shares traded at, in kobo, as a decimal string, before charges. It's exact when it has 12 decimal places or fewer, and otherwise rounded to 12. Null until a share has traded, or when we don't have the exchange's prices for the fills. |
| `OrderEstimate` | `price_kobo` | The limit price in kobo. Null for a market order. |
| `OrderEstimate` | `estimated_total_kobo` | The broker's estimate of the order's total, rounded to the whole kobo against the customer. For a buy, what the order would cost, rounded up. For a sell, what you'd receive, rounded down. In the sandbox, a buy includes 1.5% charges and a sell is net of them. The estimate is indicative, not a quote. |
| `OrderEstimate` | `estimated_total_kobo_decimal` | The broker's estimate of the order's total, in kobo, as an exact decimal string, because the broker's charges can include fractions of a kobo. `estimated_total_kobo` is this figure rounded up for a buy and down for a sell. |
| `WalletTransfer` | `amount_kobo` | The amount that moved. Always positive. |
| `WalletTransfer` | `available_change_kobo` | What the entry did to `available_kobo`: positive for a credit, a void, and a released or returned withdrawal; negative for a reserve and a held withdrawal; zero for a post and a paid withdrawal, which move money already set aside. |
| `Wallet` | `credited_kobo` | The total credited by your confirmed payments. |
| `Wallet` | `allocated_kobo` | The amount booked into your accounts at the broker. |
| `Wallet` | `reserved_kobo` | The amount in allocations we've sent that aren't yet confirmed as booked. |
| `Wallet` | `withdrawing_kobo` | The amount set aside for withdrawals we've recorded and not yet paid. |
| `Wallet` | `withdrawn_kobo` | The amount paid out to your payout account, less any your bank sent back. |
| `Wallet` | `available_kobo` | The amount you can allocate or withdraw now. |
| `AllocationRequest` | `amount_kobo` | The amount in kobo, as a whole number: at least 1 kobo, and at most ₦100,000,000. The broker doesn't publish a minimum of its own. If the broker refuses an amount, the allocation comes back `allocation_rejected` with `reject_reason` `invalid_amount`. |
| `Allocation` | `amount_kobo` | The amount, in kobo. |
| `Balance` | `opening_kobo` | The account's opening balance, as the broker defines it, rounded down to the whole kobo. Can be negative. |
| `Balance` | `opening_kobo_decimal` | The account's opening balance, in kobo, as an exact decimal string. Can be negative. |
| `Balance` | `pending_debits_kobo` | Money the broker is holding against the account, as the broker defines it, rounded up to the whole kobo. In the sandbox, the cash held for open buy orders, charges included. Never negative. |
| `Balance` | `pending_debits_kobo_decimal` | Money the broker is holding against the account, in kobo, as an exact decimal string. Never negative. |
| `Balance` | `available_kobo` | What the account can spend, as the broker defines it, rounded down to the whole kobo. In the sandbox, `opening_kobo_decimal` minus `pending_debits_kobo_decimal`. Can be negative. |
| `Balance` | `available_kobo_decimal` | What the account can spend, in kobo, as an exact decimal string. Can be negative. |
| `Position` | `average_cost_kobo_decimal` | The average price paid per share, in kobo, as an exact decimal string, because an average can include fractions of a kobo. This is the broker's figure. The broker doesn't say whether it includes charges; in the sandbox it doesn't. |
| `Position` | `market_price_kobo` | The broker's current price per share, in kobo. Null when the broker gives no price. |
| `Position` | `market_value_kobo` | `quantity` times `market_price_kobo`, in kobo. Null when `market_price_kobo` is null. |
| `Trade` | `price_kobo` | The price per share this trade filled at, in kobo. |
| `ContractNote` | `price_kobo` | The price per share, in kobo. |
| `ContractNote` | `amount_kobo` | The broker's `amount` for the trade, in kobo, rounded to the whole kobo: up on a buy, down on a sell. The broker doesn't define this figure; in the sandbox it equals `consideration_kobo`. To see what the trade cost or paid, use `consideration_kobo` and the three charges. |
| `ContractNote` | `amount_kobo_decimal` | The broker's `amount` for the trade, in kobo, as an exact decimal string. |
| `ContractNote` | `commission_kobo` | The broker's commission, in kobo, rounded up to the whole kobo. |
| `ContractNote` | `commission_kobo_decimal` | The broker's commission, in kobo, as an exact decimal string, because a charge can include fractions of a kobo. |
| `ContractNote` | `statutory_fees_kobo` | Statutory charges, in kobo, as the broker reports them, rounded up to the whole kobo. |
| `ContractNote` | `statutory_fees_kobo_decimal` | Statutory charges, in kobo, as an exact decimal string. |
| `ContractNote` | `other_fees_kobo` | Other charges, in kobo, as the broker reports them, rounded up to the whole kobo. |
| `ContractNote` | `other_fees_kobo_decimal` | Other charges, in kobo, as an exact decimal string. |
| `ContractNote` | `consideration_kobo` | The value of the shares traded, in kobo: the quantity times the price, before commission and charges, rounded to the whole kobo: up on a buy, down on a sell. In the sandbox, a buy's `consideration_kobo`, `commission_kobo`, `statutory_fees_kobo` and `other_fees_kobo` add up to what the account paid, to the nearest kobo, and a sale's `consideration_kobo` less the three charges is what it received. The broker doesn't specify how its fields add up. Add the `_kobo_decimal` figures for an exact total: each whole-kobo figure is rounded on its own. |
| `ContractNote` | `consideration_kobo_decimal` | The value of the shares traded, in kobo, as an exact decimal string. |

## Values

New values can be added to any of these lists. Treat one you don't recognise with a safe default.

| List | Values |
|---|---|
| `DocumentState` | `delivered` |
| `DocumentType` | `photo`, `government_id`, `utility_bill`, `signature` |
| `OrderState` | `sending`, `pending`, `partially_filled`, `filled`, `uncertain`, `rejected`, `refused`, `cancelled`, `expired` |
| `OrderSide` | `buy`, `sell` |
| `OrderType` | `limit`, `market` |
| `TimeInForce` | `day`, `gtc`, `ioc`, `fok` |
| `OrderRejectReason` | `insufficient_funds`, `market_closed`, `settlement_lockout`, `etf_limit_orders_only`, `limit_orders_etf_only`, `unknown_symbol`, `symbol_not_tradable`, `account_not_at_broker`, `rejected_by_exchange`, `null` |
| `EventType` | `allocation.booked`, `allocation.refused`, `allocation.rejected`, `allocation.uncertain`, `application.documents_required`, `application.opened`, `application.refused`, `application.rejected`, `application.submitted`, `application.uncertain`, `application.unplaced`, `order.cancelled`, `order.expired`, `order.filled`, `order.partially_filled`, `order.pending`, `order.refused`, `order.rejected`, `order.uncertain` |
| `Gender` | `M`, `F` |
| `ApplicationState` | `sending`, `documents_required`, `submitted`, `opened`, `uncertain`, `rejected`, `refused`, `unplaced` |
| `ApplicationRejectReason` | `invalid_field`, `already_at_broker`, `rejected_by_broker`, `declined_by_broker`, `null` |
| `WalletTransferType` | `credit`, `reserve`, `post`, `void`, `withdrawal_held`, `withdrawal_paid`, `withdrawal_released`, `withdrawal_returned` |
| `AllocationState` | `sending`, `booked`, `uncertain`, `rejected`, `refused` |
| `AllocationRejectReason` | `invalid_amount`, `closed_financial_year`, `account_not_at_broker`, `rejected_by_broker`, `settlement_lockout`, `not_booked`, `null` |
| `ChoiceKind` | `bank`, `state`, `lga` |
